strengths: The paper addresses an important and timely problem in autonomous driving: bridging the gap between geometrically consistent Bird's-Eye View (BEV) representations and the high-level semantic reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs).

The comparative study of visual representations (Section 3) provides rigorous and insightful empirical evidence that BEV tokens offer significant advantages over multi-view perspective tokens for cross-view spatial reasoning in LLMs (e.g., +46.0% accuracy on Ego3D).

The proposed semantic distillation framework (BEVLM) is elegant and practical: it transfers semantic commonsense from frozen LLMs into the BEV encoder via VQA objectives while maintaining spatial geometry with detection supervision, requiring no heavy LLM computation at inference time.

Comprehensive experimental validation on both open-loop (nuScenes) and closed-loop safety-critical benchmarks (NeuroNCAP), showing consistent improvements across two distinct end-to-end driving frameworks (UniAD and VAD).
Thoughtful ablation studies comparing against meaningful baselines (e.g., randomly initialized auxiliary heads, VLM-AD style CLIP alignment, and different pooling/projector configurations).
weaknesses: Both UniAD and VAD rely on the same BEVFormer-based deformable attention architecture; validating the distillation mechanism on structurally different BEV encoders (such as Lift-Splat-Shoot / BEVDet or Sparse4D-style representations) would significantly strengthen the claim of architecture generality.

The distillation relies heavily on the human-annotated DriveLM-nuScenes dataset. Exploring scalable pseudo-labeling or larger-scale auto-generated driving VQA datasets would better demonstrate the scaling behavior of the approach.

strengths: Compelling and well-motivated premise: Investigating whether Bird's-Eye View (BEV) representations offer superior spatial reasoning for LLMs compared to multi-view perspective image tokens directly addresses a fundamental challenge in vision-language autonomous driving.

Rigorously conducted representation study: The comparative experiments on single-view (DriveLM) and cross-view (Ego3D) spatial reasoning clearly demonstrate the representational benefits of BEV features over perspective-view tokens (e.g., +46% MCQ accuracy on Ego3D over perspective features).

Effective semantic distillation paradigm: Distilling high-level reasoning and safety semantics from a frozen LLM teacher back into the BEV encoder via ego-centric VQA tasks—while retaining geometric structure via joint detection supervision—is neat, intuitive, and effective.

Comprehensive downstream and closed-loop evaluation: The method is validated on both open-loop nuScenes planning and closed-loop safety-critical scenarios via the NeuroNCAP benchmark across two mainstream pipelines (UniAD and VAD), showing tangible gains in safety scores and impact velocities.

Extensive ablations and baseline comparisons: The inclusion of random auxiliary heads, CLIP-based feature alignment (VLM-AD style), downsampling variants, and question-category ablations provides strong evidence that gains stem from LLM semantics rather than superficial multi-task regularization.
weaknesses: Limited architectural diversity: The experimental validation is restricted to BEVFormer-style spatiotemporal transformer encoders (shared by UniAD and VAD). Exploring lift-splat-shoot (LSS) or depth-distribution-based BEV encoders (e.g., BEVDet/BEVFusion) would further substantiate the generalizability of the findings.

Dependence on human-curated VQA data: The distillation relies on DriveLM-nuScenes, which has fixed annotations and limited vocabulary/diversity compared to web-scale pre-training data, somewhat constraining the open-world semantic potential.
Sample size of Ego3D evaluation: The cross-view evaluation split from Ego3D used in Table 3 comprises only 162 test questions, which represents a relatively modest benchmark size.

High computational requirement: Distillation requires significant compute (~100 GPU hours on 8× A100 for an 8B model for just 1 epoch), which could pose practical hurdles for scaling to larger corpora without aggressive token pruning or lightweight distillation objectives.

strengths: Clear motivation and systematic study: The paper tackles a well-identified limitation in autonomous driving foundation models—namely, that standard Vision-Language Models (VLMs) process multi-view perspective images independently (sacrificing 3D geometric coherence), whereas Bird's-Eye View (BEV) representations lack rich semantic pre-training. The comparative study between perspective tokens and BEV tokens on DriveLM and Ego3D offers valuable empirical insights into cross-view spatial reasoning.

Practical and inference-efficient formulation: By using the pre-trained LLM strictly as an offline teacher to distill semantic knowledge into the BEV encoder (and regularizing with detection loss), the heavy LLM can be discarded at inference time. This allows downstream end-to-end (E2E) planners (e.g., UniAD, VAD) to benefit from semantic cues without incurring real-time inference latency.

Comprehensive evaluation across open-loop and closed-loop settings: Rather than relying solely on open-loop displacement metrics (nuScenes L2), the authors benchmark on the closed-loop NeuroNCAP safety suite across 50 runs, showing tangible improvements in safety score and collision severity reduction in critical corner cases.

Sound control experiments: The inclusion of controlled baselines—specifically the randomly initialized auxiliary transformer head and the VLM-AD CLIP-style distillation baseline—effectively verifies that the observed gains stem from pre-trained LLM semantic supervision rather than simply adding auxiliary parameters or multi-task losses.
weaknesses: Incremental algorithmic novelty: The technical formulation of 'semantic distillation' corresponds essentially to fine-tuning the BEV encoder and projector end-to-end via the standard autoregressive next-token prediction loss of a frozen VLM/LLM alongside an auxiliary detection loss. The conceptual framing as representation distillation does not introduce significant methodological innovation over standard visual instruction tuning applied to BEV tokens.

Omission of core perception benchmarks: While the paper evaluates planning L2 error and NeuroNCAP scores, it does not report standard 3D perception metrics (such as mAP and NDS on nuScenes). Given that semantic distillation reshapes the BEV feature space and uses detection only as a regularizer, it is critical to quantify whether fundamental geometric perception (3D object detection, tracking, map segmentation) is preserved or degraded.

Limited diversity of BEV encoder architectures: All experiments rely on BEVFormer-based feature extractors (shared by UniAD and VAD). Validating the approach on fundamentally different BEV paradigms—such as Lift-Splat-Shoot (LSS)-based architectures (e.g., BEVDet/BEVFusion) or purely sparse query-based representations—would be necessary to confirm the generalizability of the findings.

High variance in closed-loop safety metrics: In Table 4, the standard deviations on NeuroNCAP metrics are notably large (e.g., Collision Rate of 0.47 ± 0.30 vs. baseline 0.56 ± 0.31 for UniAD; score of 3.05 ± 1.26 vs. 2.38 ± 1.52). While the mean values show improvement, the high variance makes the statistical significance of collision avoidance less conclusive, with much of the gain driven by reduced impact velocity (crash severity) rather than avoiding collisions entirely.

Reliance on curated VQA annotations: The distillation relies directly on human-curated DriveLM-nuScenes question-answer pairs. Because this dataset is built on the same underlying nuScenes sequences, it remains unclear whether the BEV representation genuinely acquires open-world commonsense or simply fits the specific question-answering distribution of the benchmark.

strengths: Clear motivation and well-scoped problem: The paper tackles a timely and fundamental challenge in autonomous driving—reconciling the spatially disjoint nature of multi-view 2D vision foundation models with the geometrically structured yet semantically sparse nature of Bird's-Eye View (BEV) representations.

Insightful comparative representation study: The experimental comparison between perspective tokens (both foundation ViT and CNN backbone) and BEV tokens on cross-view spatial reasoning (Ego3D) provides clear empirical evidence that unified BEV representations offer substantial benefits for multi-camera 3D spatial reasoning.

Meaningful closed-loop safety evaluation: Rather than relying solely on open-loop imitation metrics (nuScenes L2 trajectory error), the authors thoroughly evaluate on the closed-loop NeuroNCAP benchmark. The results demonstrate tangible improvements in safety metrics (29% improvement in NeuroNCAP score and reduced collision severity/impact velocity).

Detailed ablation and qualitative analysis: The paper includes useful ablations investigating BEV token downsampling strategies and the specific impact of different VQA supervision subsets (showing behavior/planning queries provide the greatest safety benefit), supported by clear qualitative trajectories and collision analysis.
weaknesses: Conceptual framing vs. implementation of 'distillation': The method is framed as latent representation distillation via an LLM semantic manifold (Eq. 1), but the actual implementation is essentially standard multi-task cross-modal instruction tuning/pre-training (next-token prediction cross-entropy loss alongside 3D detection loss) through a frozen LLM and trainable BEV encoder + MLP projector.

Limited architectural exploration: The framework is demonstrated almost exclusively on the deformable-attention-based BEVFormer/UniAD architecture. While computational constraints are acknowledged in the appendix, validating whether these findings generalize to Lift-Splat-Shoot (LSS)-based architectures (e.g., BEVDepth, BEVFusion) would significantly strengthen the empirical claim.

Reliance on human-annotated driving VQA data: The semantic enhancement is trained directly on DriveLM-nuScenes, which is human-curated. This somewhat limits the claim of tapping into the unbounded open-world knowledge of LLMs, as the semantics transferred are largely bounded by the human annotations of DriveLM.

Small test set size for cross-view reasoning: The Ego3D test split consists of only 162 question instances (Table 8), which is relatively small and can introduce variance into the cross-view reasoning metrics.

strengths: Compelling Motivation and Problem Formulation: The paper clearly identifies and addresses a critical trade-off in autonomous driving: while multi-view perspective VLM architectures possess semantic richness but struggle with geometric coherence across cameras, BEV encoders offer structured 3D spatial consistency but suffer from purely geometric supervision.

Systematic Visual Representation Comparison: The paper provides a well-controlled empirical comparison between perspective tokens (ViT, FPN backbone) and BEV tokens on spatial question-answering tasks (DriveLM and cross-view Ego3D). The findings effectively demonstrate that compact BEV representations can achieve superior cross-view spatial reasoning compared to much larger perspective vision backbones.

Practical Deployment Paradigm: Instead of requiring an LLM/VLA to run online in the vehicle's control loop—which introduces severe latency, compute, and reliability issues—the proposed method distills LLM semantics into the BEV encoder offline, allowing standard, efficient E2E planning stacks (UniAD) to benefit from semantic reasoning at inference time.

Comprehensive Evaluation Beyond Open-Loop Metrics: Recognizing the known pitfalls of open-loop imitation metrics, the authors evaluate on the closed-loop NeuroNCAP benchmark in safety-critical corner cases. The analysis of collision rates, safety scores, and impact velocity provides meaningful evidence that semantic distillation aids safety-aware decision-making.
weaknesses: Incremental Methodological Novelty: While the concept is framed as 'representation distillation via latent alignment' (Eq. 1), the actual implementation is essentially standard visual instruction tuning / multi-task tuning: backpropagating the frozen LLM's cross-entropy loss through an MLP projector into the BEV encoder alongside an object detection regularization loss. The theoretical framing over-complicates what is fundamentally multi-task VQA fine-tuning.

Missing Impact on Fundamental Perception Metrics: The paper demonstrates downstream planning improvements, but does not report standard 3D perception benchmarks (e.g., nuScenes detection mAP, NDS, or tracking metrics) for the distilled BEV encoder. It remains unclear whether joint training with VQA alters low-level geometric fidelity or detection performance.

Reliance on Curated VQA Annotations: The distillation pipeline relies entirely on human-annotated driving VQA data (DriveLM). This limits scalability compared to standard foundation model pre-training, as acquiring dense, multi-step driving reasoning text at scale is prohibitively expensive.

Limited Architectural Diversity: The experiments are restricted to a single BEV backbone architecture (BEVFormer) and a single planner (UniAD). Validating the distillation across alternative representations (e.g., depth-distribution-based BEVFusion) or vector-based planners (e.g., VAD) would significantly bolster the general applicability of the framework.

strengths: Compelling and timely motivation: Bridges the gap between the semantic richness of large language models and the geometrically grounded, spatially consistent nature of Bird's-Eye View (BEV) representations in autonomous driving.

Systematic representation analysis: The empirical comparison between perspective-view visual tokens (ViT and CNN backbone) and BEV tokens on spatial reasoning benchmarks (DriveLM, Ego3D) provides clear and valuable insights, showing that BEV tokens are structurally superior for cross-view spatial reasoning.

Practical deployment design: By distilling semantic knowledge directly into the BEV encoder and subsequently freezing it for end-to-end planning (UniAD), the approach retains real-time efficiency and reliability during inference without requiring online LLM generation at test time.

Meaningful evaluation on safety-critical benchmarks: In addition to standard open-loop nuScenes trajectory evaluation, the paper demonstrates tangible gains in closed-loop simulation on NeuroNCAP (a 29% improvement in safety score and a reduction in collision rate from 62% to 55% for the 8B variant).

Thorough ablations and analysis: The paper includes useful ablations on BEV token downsampling strategies, scaling of LLM teacher size (1B vs. 8B), and the impact of different VQA supervision subsets (Perception/Prediction vs. Behavior/Planning).
weaknesses: Architectural generality is unverified experimentally: All experiments are built strictly upon the BEVFormer / UniAD architecture. While the authors rightly note the heavy compute budget in the limitations, validating the distillation across alternative BEV paradigms (e.g., LSS-based architectures like BEVDet/BEVFusion) or modern sparse planners (e.g., SparseDrive) would substantially strengthen the claims.

Slight conceptual over-framing of distillation: Section 4 formalizes the approach as latent representation distillation via alignment to an ideal token embedding $v^*$, but in practice the training is standard visual instruction tuning using language cross-entropy loss backpropagated through a frozen LLM and projector into the BEV encoder. Framing this as a fundamentally novel latent manifold distillation somewhat obscures what is essentially multi-task language-supervised pre-training/fine-tuning of the vision backbone.

Dataset scale and domain diversity: The semantic distillation relies exclusively on DriveLM-nuScenes, which is derived from the same sensor setup and driving domain as the downstream evaluation. Evaluating whether this distillation provides true open-world generalizability or robustness to out-of-distribution visual semantics remains an open question.
